title: At what angle do the diagonals of a rhombus cross?
description: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, and two triangles at the crossing match by the side side side rule. The two angles at O sit on a straight line, so each is a right angle. Keeko doubts that the angle can be the same for thin and fat rhombuses.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a rhombus cross at a right angle, because two triangles at the crossing are congruent and their angles at O add up to one hundred eighty. Watch for students who think the angle at O changes with the shape of the rhombus.

source: In rhombus GAME the diagonals meet at O, with GM = 8 cm and EA = 6 cm. Find the angle at O, GO and EO.
video_script.why: The child sees that congruent triangles at the crossing give a right angle, and that the halves of the diagonals give GO and EO.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rhombus GAME with its diagonals crossing at O
video_script.anchor: the rhombus GAME of the book with its diagonals GM and EA crossing at O
video_script.wrong_answer: the angle at O could be anything
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a thin rhombus and a fat rhombus have different angles at O, but the proof uses only equal sides and halves.
video_script.payoff_line: The diagonals meet at ninety degrees

final_answer.value: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm
final_answer.spoken: the diagonals meet at ninety degrees, G O is four centimetres, and E O is three centimetres

hold_back: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm
never_show: a right angle mark at O before step 3
maths_rules: a rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: GO = MO and EO = AO
triangle GEO and triangle MEO: GE = ME, GO = MO, EO common, so they are congruent by SSS
angle GOE = angle MOE, and together they make 180, so each is 90
video_script.design: One idea: two congruent triangles at the crossing give equal angles on a straight line, so each is a right angle. One rhombus stays on the board with both diagonals.

<bookmark mark='ninety'/>One hundred eighty divided by two gives ninety degrees for each.
<bookmark mark='go'/>Step four, G O is eight divided by two, which is four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='eo'/>E O is six divided by two, which is three centimetres.
